subtitle: Discovering Intelligent Stable Forms

sections.heading: ONE · ILLUSTRATING
sections.why: This part sets out what illustrating is for and how a drawing goes on through changing, which is this file's own subject.

sections.heading: 1.1 Illustrating changing, a form going on
sections.why: It says a drawing shows changing through a visible relation and that each drawing serves a sentence of a living file.

sections.heading: 1.2 A still and a motion
sections.why: It parts a still drawing, a fixed picture of one momentary, from a motion, faces in sequence each a next.

sections.heading: 1.3 Prior, now and next, making better and breaking
sections.why: It describes how a drawing improves or breaks and how what survives goes on to a next explaining.

sections.heading: 1.4 Self-bounding, self-orienting, self-competent
sections.why: It names the aim of the illustrating and which other files bring operations, numbers and naming to it.

sections.heading: 1.5 Living bounding and a boundary a self declares, a drawing's test
sections.why: It gives a drawing's test for any boundary a self declares, a storyboard asking whether resolving goes on under it.

sections.heading: 1.6 What a drawing leaves out
sections.why: It lists the fixings a drawing must not install, such as a common clock, a size, a place or a stored total.

sections.heading: 1.7 Forms, a still with numbers to a model in hand
sections.why: It orders the forms of illustration from a still with numbers to a physical model, each a next after the one before.

sections.heading: TWO · THE METHOD AT ITS FACES
sections.why: This part draws a self's own resolving as faces, which is a drawing of stable forms and so within the title.

sections.heading: 2.1 Six numbers, two sides, three momentaries
sections.why: It lays out the first storyboard faces of one self's resolving: six positions and three momentaries.

sections.heading: 2.2 Sixteen ways, and one that stops nowhere
sections.why: It draws the sixteen ways a next could follow a prior and a now as small squares, showing which hold a still.

sections.heading: 2.3 Four dots, an empty centre and two triangles
sections.why: It draws the parity unit square and a five-spot face with its centre left empty as a between.

sections.heading: 2.4 A table at 10, no path through until prior changes now
sections.why: It draws the twelve cells of the table at 10 as faces, three with no path through and one empty.

sections.heading: 2.5 One self, and two selves at 0
sections.why: It draws one self resolving alone and two selves sharing across with a 0 between them, so it is a self and a coupling at once.

sections.heading: 2.6 Two inversions at forty-five degrees, a right spiral step
sections.why: It draws a field's geometry of two inversions making a right spiral step and a compass face of a double angle.

sections.heading: 2.7 Ten at five places
sections.why: It draws the ten unchangeables seated at five places, each a side fixing beside a side changing.

sections.heading: 2.8 Seventeen names, bi-foldings, and a local nine
sections.why: It keeps the seventeen-name face and the local nine-dot face apart and lists the correspondence a drawing still has to find.

sections.heading: 2.9 Six diamonds and a compass face
sections.why: It describes the next-scale six-diamond picture and leaves open how its routes and angle correspond to the numbers.

sections.heading: THREE · THE NUMBERS
sections.why: This part turns relations of the number files into faces a drawing can show.

sections.heading: 3.1 Number forming, podaling and rings
sections.why: It gives number faces for podaling and rings, mostly restating Natural Numbers with views a drawing could take.

sections.heading: 3.2 A ratio alternating about φ, and two windings
sections.why: It draws a ratio swinging about φ and a φ winding that never closes, a going on with no landing.

sections.heading: 3.3 A pentagon, rectangles and an icosahedron
sections.why: It draws a field's geometry of the pentagon, three golden rectangles and the icosahedron with their counts.

sections.heading: 3.4 Two routes, a diamond, and a fold at each scale
sections.why: It draws number relations about twenty-eight, a diamond's two paths and a fold growing at each scale.

sections.heading: FOUR · SELVES AND SOCIETIES
sections.why: This part draws selves coupling into societies, using pictures such as a crowd, a dance and a lock.

sections.heading: 4.1 Tunneling, corusing and bi-folding, a towel
sections.why: It describes a depth journey inward to a corus and outward again, shown with a twisting towel.

sections.heading: 4.2 Spirals coupling across, a torus of selves, a 0 tunneling
sections.why: It draws spirals of selves and two spirals coupling across into a society and a torus of selves.

sections.heading: 4.3 Co-chaining, bi-tunneling and society
sections.why: It draws along and across couplings and a society with no hub, though its content leans on Natural Networking.

sections.heading: 4.4 Locking, a seam moving, a between releasing
sections.why: It draws two societies bi-coupling until they lock, with a field's pendulums and fireflies beside it.

sections.heading: 4.5 Co-chaining a plaza, bi-tunneling a crowd
sections.why: It draws one passage through a crowd and the crowd's openings as two views of one changing.

sections.heading: 4.6 Swaying and going along, a moving snake
sections.why: It parts a snake's sway, a bend going along its body and the whole snake going along, as a field's picture of one body.

sections.heading: 4.7 Bi-folding, around and across stitching
sections.why: It draws a lockstitch as a field's mechanical making that shows around and across together.

sections.heading: 4.8 Co-discovering, multiperson jigsaw puzzling
sections.why: It draws people sharing a puzzle so that one fit makes a next fit discoverable, which is both sharing and discovering.

sections.heading: 4.9 Bi-inversioning-co-recursioning, two swimmers inverting at one meeting
sections.why: It draws two swimmers inverting off each other at one meeting, a mutual coupling of two selves.

sections.heading: 4.10 A walking pair, a dance and a conversation
sections.why: It draws a walking pair, a dance and a conversation as two sides taking turns with no hub.

sections.heading: 4.11 A cube and open rings
sections.why: It draws a puzzle cube as a form with no still term and compares it with open rings, a comparison still open.

sections.heading: FIVE · THE SCIENCES' PICTURES
sections.why: This part sets familiar science pictures beside a file's sentence and shows which still each picture installs.

sections.heading: 5.1 Atoms, electrons, bonds and molecules
sections.why: It reads pictures of atoms, bonds, benzene and the periodic table against Natural Physics and Natural Chemistry.

sections.heading: 5.2 Light, spin and a click
sections.why: It reads pictures of light, polarizers, a spinor, a double slit and Bell tests against their files.

sections.heading: 5.3 Cosmos
sections.why: It reads pictures of light cones, black holes, orbits, an expanding universe and three bodies against their files.

sections.heading: 5.4 Earth, matter and phases
sections.why: It reads pictures of wells, phase diagrams, chemical patterns, faults, entropy and a tokamak against their files.

sections.heading: 5.5 Brains
sections.why: It reads pictures of a firing neuron, a synapse, sleep, a slime mould and other minds against their files.

sections.heading: 5.6 Bodies and life
sections.why: It reads pictures of a heartbeat, DNA, regrowth, rhythms, folding, ageing and flocks against their files.

sections.heading: SIX · HUMAN SOCIETY'S PICTURES
sections.why: This part sets familiar pictures of human society beside a file's sentence and shows which still each installs.

sections.heading: 6.1 A clock, a vote and a crowd behind a centre
sections.why: It reads a common clock, a ballot and a leader with followers as pictures that install a hub or a centre.

sections.heading: 6.2 A market, a ledger and a food web
sections.why: It reads supply and demand curves, a balance sheet and a food pyramid as pictures that install a still point or a total.

sections.heading: 6.3 A network, a hierarchy and many paintings
sections.why: It reads a hub network, an org chart and a master diagram as pictures that install a hub, a root or one painting.

sections.heading: SEVEN · THE TEN AS PICTURES
sections.why: This part turns each of the ten unchangeables into a familiar drawing with a resolving drawn beside it.

sections.heading: 7.1 Ten drawings, one resolving
sections.why: It gives one familiar picture for each of the ten unchangeables and says how to draw a self inverting beside it.

sections.heading: EIGHT · EXPRESSING
sections.why: This part lists existing images, further views and new ways to express forms, which is illustrating going on.

sections.heading: 8.1 Existing imagery and its explaining going on
sections.why: It lists existing images and studies with what each keeps and what still needs improving.

sections.heading: 8.2 Further views through nature and living
sections.why: It lists further pictures from nature and living still to draw, each with the file it would serve.

sections.heading: 8.3 A resolver society as a surface that animates
sections.why: It proposes letting a society of selves executing code draw itself on a screen, a society and a method going on together.

sections.heading: 8.4 Three dimensions, a model in hand and a society at a material
sections.why: Its main body is about a robot swarm and a society of selves working a material, which the section itself says is Natural Engineering's subject.
sections.home: Natural Engineering: Engineering Bi-Moral-Co-Agency at a Substrate

sections.heading: NINE · CO-IMPROVING
sections.why: This part says how the file couples with other files and receives new illustrations.

sections.heading: 9.1 Files coupling, contributions going on
sections.why: It lists what each other living file gives to the illustrating and receives back from it.

sections.heading: 9.2 Receiving an illustration, and its kit
sections.why: Its subject is how incoming material enters a file and what the improving kit holds, which is the subject of bringing incoming value into each file.
sections.home: Geodesic Improving Method: Bringing Incoming Value into Each File, Prior, Now and Next

sections.heading: 9.3 Not yet at files
sections.why: It lists familiar pictures that no living file yet has a sentence for, which are open places for this file.

summary: Of 57 parts and sections, 55 are within the title and subtitle and 2 are outside: 8.4, whose robot-swarm body belongs to Natural Engineering, and 9.2, whose intake process belongs to Geodesic Improving Method. The file is mostly observing, because Parts TWO, THREE, FIVE, SIX and SEVEN draw a self's resolving, number relations and the stills that familiar pictures install, with possibling in Part FOUR and discovering in Parts ONE, EIGHT and NINE. The clearest holes are the pictures 9.3 says no living file has a sentence for (galaxy spiral arms, a golden angle, a tree of life, a tensegrity dome, lightning), and the correspondences the file says are still unexpressed: the local nine to the seventeen names, the six diamonds to the two routes, the cube to the open rings, the unexecuted three-phase lock, and whether sixty is a position or a between.
